prompt: Compare the main ASIC mining firmware providers: dev fees, supported models, key features.
answer_text:
The main ASIC mining firmware providers most often compared today are **Braiins OS+**, **VNish**, and **LuxOS**. Their biggest differences are **dev fee**, **hardware support**, and whether they emphasize *auto-tuning, pool integration, or fleet management*.[1][2][9]

| Provider | Dev fee | Supported models | Key features |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **Braiins OS+** | **2–2.5%** | Primarily **Bitmain Antminer** models from **S9 through S21**, including S19/S19 Pro/S19j Pro/S19k Pro/S19 XP/S21/S21 XP variants; not listed for Whatsminer in the comparison result.[1][9] | **Per-chip, continuous auto-tuning**, **native Stratum V2** support, pool-agnostic operation, strong download verification with published hashes/GPG.[1][2][9] |
| **VNish** | **2–2.8%** | Broad **Antminer S9 through S21** support; also **Whatsminer M30, M50, M60** series per the comparison result.[1][2] | **Per-chip, profile-based auto-tuning**, broad compatibility, monitoring tied to official builds, no Stratum V2 support listed in the comparison result.[1][2] |
| **LuxOS** | **2.8%** | **Antminer S19 and S21 only** in the comparison result.[1][7] | **Per-chip, continuous auto-tuning**, designed for larger operations and commonly positioned around Luxor’s mining ecosystem; no Stratum V2 support listed in the comparison result.[1][3][7] |

A few practical takeaways:
- **Lowest listed dev fee among these three:** **Braiins OS+** at **2–2.5%**.[1][9]
- **Broadest model coverage:** **VNish**, because it spans both Bitmain Antminers and some MicroBT Whatsminer series.[1][2][7]
- **Best-known protocol feature:** **Braiins OS+** because it has **native Stratum V2** support.[1][9]
- **Most limited compatibility in the comparison:** **LuxOS**, which is shown as focused on **S19/S21** hardware.[1][7]
